hypotheses.justification: The statement holds for any ϖ : 𝒪[L]. The same file proves `TauCeti.smul_div_mem_unitFiltration` (line 213): for σ ∈ ramificationGroup G 𝒪[L] (i : ℤ) and any units y z : Lˣ with (z : L) = σ • (y : L) / (y : L), we have z ∈ unitFiltration L i. It needs only hσ and picks its own uniformizer via `IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_irreducible`. Proof without hϖ: split on (ϖ : L) = 0. If (ϖ : L) = 0, then hy gives (y : L) = σ • 0 / 0 = 0, which contradicts y.ne_zero, so this case is vacuous. Otherwise apply `smul_div_mem_unitFiltration hσ (y := Units.mk0 (ϖ : L) h) hy`. That theorem currently calls this one for its chosen irreducible ϖ, so to avoid circularity keep the present proof (with hϖ) as a private lemma and use it in both `smul_div_mem_unitFiltration` and the hϖ-free version. The general fact is also true mathematically: write ϖ = π^k·u; σπ/π lies in U(L,i) and σu/u lies in U(L,i+1), and the unit filtration is a subgroup.
